summary: Protect new person pairing codes from offline guessing with a member-local keyed verifier and independent random pairing identities.

replay.detail: No claim replay or rebuild. Existing completed person pairings remain usable; pending legacy challenges are accepted only while unexpired and when expiry minus claim timestamp is at most 300000 ms.

schema.detail: New custom.client.pairing-begun claims add verifier: hmac-sha256-v1 and verifier_key_id: SHA256(secret); code_hash stores HMAC-SHA-256 rather than an unkeyed code digest. MAC input: domain bytes fractal/pairing-code-verifier/v1 (no NUL), the full prefixed pairing ID's UTF-8 bytes, then the code's UTF-8 bytes, each prefixed by its byte length as an unsigned big-endian u32, without normalization. Verifiers are bound to their stored pairing ID including its namespace prefix. Pairing IDs and begin-claim subjects use independent random 128-bit values; device ID derivation is unchanged. The member-local secret is stored at state_dir/pairing-verifier/key with mode 0600 and parent directory mode 0700, never in claims or backups.

compatibility.detail: Person pairing request and response shapes are unchanged. A missing or changed verifier key, or a legacy challenge lifetime exceeding 300 seconds, returns additive HTTP 403 pairing-restart-required, retryable false, with message start pairing again. Incorrect codes with the matching key retain forbidden. Replicated claims alone do not permit offline guessing against the keyed verifier; the code still has only 40 bits of entropy and a 300-second expiry. This change does not replace encrypted transport or independent person-root fingerprint verification and does not change external assistant pairing.

downtime.detail: No restart-time migration or rebuild. Ordinary restarts retaining the same secret preserve still-live pending challenges.

manual.detail: Keep the member-local verifier secret private and out of claim backups. After restoring claims without the original secret, or generating or rotating a secret, begin pending pairings again on the intended member. A pairing-restart-required refusal cannot be recovered by retrying the old code; legacy challenges with lifetimes longer than 300 seconds must also be restarted. Binary downgrade: a pre-keyed-verifier binary ignores the verifier marker and compares code_hash with the unkeyed code digest, so in-flight keyed pairings fail with HTTP 403 forbidden and message the pairing code is invalid, expired, or already used (not pairing-restart-required). Start those pairings again on the downgraded member. No stored claims or verifier state need cleanup.

recovery.detail: Start a fresh pairing after a claim-only restore or verifier-secret loss or replacement. There is intentionally no rollback protection when both secret and claims are restored together to an earlier state: a previously consumed challenge may become usable again until its original expiry. Such a restore does not preserve single-use history.
